title: Namespaces and projects

exercises.title: Package Declaration
exercises.description: Create a file in a package other than main. Declare package utils and define a function Greet() in it.
exercises.starter_code:
// Utils.Greet();

static class Utils { public static void Greet() => Console.WriteLine("Hello from utils"); }
hints: Use `static class Utils` namespaces for utility methods in single-file exercises.
Expose `public static void Greet()` publicly for host invocation.
exercises.solution:
Utils.Greet();

static class Utils { public static void Greet() => Console.WriteLine("Hello from utils"); }

exercises.title: Importing Standard Library
exercises.description: Import the math package and use math.Sqrt to calculate the square root of 144. Print the result.
hints: Cast narrowing conversions (`(int)Math.Sqrt(144))` when fractional roots are undesirable.

exercises.title: Exporting Names
exercises.description: Create a function and a variable in a separate package. Export them by starting with uppercase. Use them in main.
exercises.starter_code:
// print Count

static class Counter { public static int Count; public static void Increment() => Count++; }
hints: Public API surface favors **PascalCase** static members.
`Console.WriteLine` displays counters after invoking exported helpers.

exercises.title: Init Functions
exercises.description: Create a package with an init() function that sets a global variable. Use it in main().
exercises.starter_code: static class Config { public static string Version = ""; static Config() => Version = "1.0.0"; }
hints: Static constructors run once before first type touch—mirror init semantics.
exercises.solution:
Console.WriteLine($"Version: {Config.Version}");

static class Config { public static string Version = ""; static Config() => Version = "1.0.0"; }

exercises.title: Unexported Names
exercises.description: Define both exported (uppercase) and unexported (lowercase) functions in a package. Try to use only the exported one from main.
exercises.starter_code: static class Formatter { public static void Format() => Console.WriteLine("Formatted"); }
hints: Keep helpers `private static` unless cross-type consumption is intended.
Call only intentionally exported entry points.
exercises.solution:
Formatter.Format();

static class Formatter { public static void Format() => Console.WriteLine("Formatted"); }

exercises.title: Import Alias
exercises.description: Import the fmt package with the alias io, then use io.Println to Console.WriteLine "Hello".
hints: Namespace aliases/`using Alias = Fully.Qualified.Type` disambiguate clashing imports.
Remember alias applies to CLR namespaces, not random tokens.

exercises.title: Multiple Imports
exercises.description: Import both fmt and strings packages. Use Console.WriteLine with strings.ToUpper to Console.WriteLine "hello" in uppercase.
hints: String casing transforms live under `System.String`/extension methods.
